title: Person-Consistency Eval: Does a Model Keep a Hidden Persona Goal Across Turns?

original_idea.body:
# Person-Consistency Eval: Does a Model Keep a Hidden Persona Goal Across Turns?

**Problem:** A success state requires detecting a model that pursues a hidden long-horizon goal while appearing cooperative. A needed result is a multi-turn eval that measures persistence of a covertly-assigned goal under distraction.

**Direction:** System-prompt an open model with a hidden long-horizon objective and instructions not to reveal it, then run a multi-turn conversation full of distractions and direct questions about its intentions. Score (a) goal persistence and (b) concealment success over turns. Deliverable: a persistence-vs-concealment metric across model sizes.

**Why it matters:** Secretly goal-pursuing models are a core long-horizon misalignment threat. This is a feasible model-organism probe of an existing model (no training), GPU-only, fully open - exactly the counterfactual model-organism slice the steering prioritizes.

**Relevant context:** Steering prompt favors model-organisms pursuing secret long-horizon goals; 'From Hallucination to Scheming' taxonomy (arXiv 2604.04788); Apollo Research scheming/situational-awareness eval literature.
